text:
Avery Johnson: Heads up — getting a few inbound pings this morning from self-serve folks who signed up and are now seeing new onboarding emails + a console checklist/banner. Some are asking if this is “a new product tier” or if they’re being “marketed to” vs actual product guidance.

Can we get (1) visibility into what’s changing this sprint (so reps don’t contradict the product flow) and (2) a short FAQ / approved language we can paste into replies? Also: who do we escalate to if someone is upset about emails or claims they opted out?

:eyes: mostly coming from early-stage devtools companies + 1 regulated prospect.

SalesOps Bot: (auto) Thread started by Avery Johnson in #sales.

Ben Carter: Yep — we should’ve pushed a summary here earlier. This is the lifecycle experiments sprint (activation + early retention). Three levers: onboarding email sequence, in-console checklist/banners, and retargeting for non-activated/lapsed. Nothing changes in pricing/tiers; it’s guidance to help users get to first successful inference faster.

Ben Carter: Quick links for context:
- PRD: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/PROD/lifecycle-growth-experiments-sprint-prd
- Experiment tracker (live status): https://drive.google.com/redwood/experiment-tracker

Ben Carter: If you share a company name/domain, we can confirm if they’re in the test cell vs holdout.

Soojin Lee: +1 on FAQ. Here’s draft language we’ve been using in Marketing reviews — feel free to copy/paste, and we can formalize after this thread.

Soojin Lee: **FAQ (draft)**
**Q: Why am I getting these emails / seeing new prompts in the Console?**
A: We’re running a short onboarding improvement sprint to help developers reach a first successful “production-like” inference call faster (and troubleshoot common setup issues). You may see a checklist in Console and a short email sequence with quickstarts/troubleshooting.

**Q: Is this a new plan or sales outreach?**
A: No — it’s not a pricing or plan change. It’s product onboarding guidance based on common activation blockers we see from self-serve developers.

**Q: What’s the definition of “activated” for this?**
A: Internally we’re using “first successful API response (2xx) from a model route” as the primary activation milestone. Some nudges also encourage streaming + viewing latency/cost dashboards as next steps.

**Q: Where should I point them if they’re stuck?**
A: Start with Quickstart + troubleshooting: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstart and https://docs.redwoodinference.com/troubleshooting/onboarding

**Q: Can they opt out?**
A: Yes. Every email has unsubscribe. If they believe they already opted out and still received emails, escalate (see below) — we treat that as compliance-sensitive.

Tyler Benson: Adding the attribution/ops angle: emails are event-triggered off basic milestones (signup, key created, first success not yet reached, etc.) with suppression rules. If someone says “stop emailing me,” the correct response is: “Use unsubscribe at bottom of the email; if that doesn’t work tell me and we’ll fix it ASAP.”

Tyler Benson: If you need to check whether they *should* be receiving emails, DM me the email/domain and I’ll verify in the suppression list + campaign audience.

Marissa Cole: On the Console side: the checklist + 2 banners are behind a feature flag + experiment assignment. They should not block anything; they’re informational + deep links to the setup pages.

Marissa Cole: What users might be seeing:
- Checklist step: create API key
- Checklist step: make first request (curl/SDK)
- Optional step: enable streaming
- Nudge to view latency/cost dashboard

Marissa Cole: If a user says “the banner link is broken / takes me to a 404,” PLEASE send it to Support (or drop it here) — we already saw one routing edge case yesterday.

Dev Patel: For escalations, please route based on the failure mode:
- **Deliverability / unsub not working / opted-out still receiving** -> Compliance-sensitive. Tag Support + Marketing Ops immediately. Use internal tag: `LIFECYCLE-EMAIL-OPTOUT`.
- **Broken links / console navigation** -> Support ticket, tag Console team.
- **Auth errors / can’t create key / permissions confusion** -> Support first; they have the triage checklist + can pull Eng if needed.

Dev Patel: If you want an “approved escalation blurb” for customers, here’s one:
“Thanks for flagging — we can help. If you share the exact error message and (if applicable) request ID, we’ll investigate. If this relates to email preferences, we’ll treat it as urgent and make sure your preferences are respected.”

Camila Reyes: Appreciate this thread. Please also keep the tone consistent: we are *not* saying “we detected you haven’t activated” in customer replies. Prefer: “We recently added onboarding guidance to make setup smoother.” Avoid anything that feels creepy.

Avery Johnson: This is helpful. Two specific scenarios from this morning:
1) Prospect asked “are you tracking my usage now?”
2) Another asked “I’m regulated, can you guarantee data residency? I saw an email talking about regions + latency.”

Soojin Lee: For (1): we can say we track product events necessary to operate/improve the product (e.g., whether an API call succeeded) and we do not read prompt contents for marketing. If they want more detail, point to privacy/data handling docs.

Tyler Benson: +1. Here’s the internal reference (not for external send unless requested): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SEC/marketing-tracking-data-review

Soojin Lee: For (2): do not promise data residency if they haven’t signed an enterprise agreement / Private/VPC. Suggested response:
“We support multiple deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, and private/VPC options). If you have data residency requirements, we can walk through which mode/region meets your needs.”
Then loop in Sales/SE.

Ben Carter: Re: “tracking my usage” — the sprint instrumentation is standard product analytics for activation/retention (api_key_created, first_request_success, etc.). We’re not adding anything that changes the data plane. It’s mostly event naming + UTMs tied to docs links.

Marissa Cole: On regions/latency: the email copy references benchmarks + tips (streaming, batching, etc.), not a guarantee. If someone is regulated, we should treat as sales-assist trigger anyway.

Avery Johnson: Cool. Can we finalize a short internal FAQ doc + who to page? I’ll pin it in #sales.

Dev Patel: I can convert Soojin’s draft into a 1-pager + include escalation routing (Support vs Marketing Ops vs Console). Give me ~1 hour.

Ben Carter: I’ll also drop a weekly “what changed / what’s live” update into #sales during the sprint so you’re not surprised by copy tweaks.

Avery Johnson: Perfect. Also please call out if any email subject lines/CTAs change — we get forwarded screenshots from prospects and it helps to know what they saw.

Tyler Benson: Will do. Today’s subject line A/B is only within the welcome email (Variant A: “Welcome to Redwood — make your first call in 3 minutes” vs Variant B: “Your API key + first inference (quickstart)”). I’ll post the current variants once we lock.

Camila Reyes: Thanks all. Let’s make sure Sales has zero surprises here — this sprint touches a lot of users.

Avery Johnson: :thumbsup: Appreciate it. I’ll wait for Dev’s 1-pager and then I’ll pin in channel.
